pronunciation.notes: The b sounds like p at the end of a word.

word.meaning: from (a point in time or place); off, away
word.shortDefinition: Marks a starting point, or something moving away.

intro.title: From now on
paragraphs: Ab is a tiny word with two jobs. On its own it marks a starting point: ab Montag, from Monday. As a prefix it means 'off' or 'away', and it's inside dozens of A1 verbs: abfahren, abholen, abgeben.

etymology.title: Where it comes from
etymology.summary: Ab is the German cousin of English 'off' and 'of'. Both once meant 'away from'.

keyTrap.title: The big trap: ab or seit?
keyTrap.explanation: Ab looks forward from a starting point. Seit looks back at something that started in the past and is still going on.

wrong.verdict: You've lived there since 2020, so it's seit.

correct.note: Started in the past, still true: seit.

correct.german: Ab Montag arbeite ich in Berlin.
correct.literal: From Monday I work in Berlin.

commonMistakes.title: As a verb prefix it splits
commonMistakes.explanation: Ab- verbs are separable, so ab goes to the end of the sentence.
commonMistakes.correct: Der Zug fährt um acht ab.

commonMistakes.title: Prices and ages
commonMistakes.explanation: Ab also means 'from … up' for prices and ages.

sampleSentences.german: Der Bus fährt um 7 Uhr ab.
Ab und zu gehe ich ins Kino.
sampleSentences.english: I go to the cinema now and then.

sampleSentences.german: Ab hier müssen Sie zu Fuß gehen.
sampleSentences.english: From here you have to walk.

memoryHook: Ab = off, away, from here on. Ab Montag looks forward; seit Montag looks back.

quiz.explanation: Started in the past and still going: seit.

quiz.prompt: ___ nächster Woche habe ich einen neuen Job.
quiz.explanation: Starting from a future point: ab.

quiz.fullAnswer: Der Zug fährt um 9 Uhr ab.
quiz.explanation: Abfahren splits; ab goes to the end.

quiz.prompt: ___ und zu trinke ich Kaffee. (now and then)
quiz.fullAnswer: Ab und zu trinke ich Kaffee.
quiz.explanation: Ab und zu: now and then.
